reason: Eight cycle-specific full SEM outputs carry non-positive first-order derivative product matrix warnings attributed by Mplus to parameters exceeding design degrees of freedom. All 18 split-cycle primary SEMs are retained as retired audit runs, with no inferential use. Replace those comparisons with 12 single-outcome pooled regressions allowing all exposure and covariate slopes and intercepts to differ by cycle. The pooled design retains 29 strata and 61 PSUs.
scope: Two age groups x two biological outcomes x three rhythm metrics, fixed before fitting replacement models.
The exposure-by-cycle coefficient is the formal cycle contrast; bG and bH are cycle-specific slopes in the pooled model, common observed-variable scale.
No cognitive/depressive indirect effects inferred from these regressions. They are diagnostic exposure–biological-measure associations, not full SEM a paths.
Outcome-specific observed samples differ from full FIML SEM samples. Models retain original covariates and do not add activity-volume adjustment.
P values are exploratory and unadjusted; the cycle contrast cannot isolate laboratory instrument effects from period differences.
